description: Who has won the most, or been paid out the most, as the site's rankings page shows it. Accounts ranked by competitions won (first place in a resolved competition's final standings), then prize money paid, then podium finishes (second or third); accounts level on all three share a rank. Counted as each account's public profile counts its record (GET /api/profiles/:handle): public entries in published competitions, places only once a competition is resolved, prize money only once paid; house entries, demo competitions and demo accounts count for nothing. Every account with a win, a podium finish or prize money paid is ranked. That is order wins, the default; order paid ranks the same accounts by prize money paid instead, then competitions won, then podium finishes. Best first, a page at a time: pass next_cursor back as cursor with the same order (a cursor pages only the order it came from; another order's is the route's 400); order names the page's order and total counts every ranked account. Each account with its rank in that order (accounts level on all three share one and are listed by handle), handle, display_name, picture (image, and avatar for an uploaded one), profile_url (its page, /u/<handle>; get_profile with the handle reads its record and its solutions) and record: the numbers its profile shows (competitions_entered, competitions_won, competitions_placed, podium_finishes, other_placements, best_placement, and prize_usd, the prize money paid in USD as a decimal string). The same answer for every caller; no build cost, tokens or models.

cursor.description: The previous page's next_cursor, for the next page (keep the other arguments the same)

order.description: wins (default): most competitions won first, then prize money paid, then podium finishes; paid: most prize money paid first, then competitions won, then podium finishes

name: list_rankings
title: List the rankings
